title: Hiroshige, Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake
lede: Travellers hurry across a high wooden bridge under black rain lines and a hand-wiped storm cloud, in Hiroshige’s One Hundred Famous Views of Edo.
summary: Diagonal bridge, fine rain lines, and a dark bokashi cloud. Utagawa Hiroshige, 1857.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the Art Institute of Chicago image of impression 1925.3742 (1686 × 2533 px).

styles.note: A canonical late landscape print: a bridge cut diagonally by the sheet edges, rain as fine key-block lines, and bokashi clouds and water.

context: AIC catalogues the sheet as a color woodblock print, ōban, 33.4 × 21.8 cm, from the series One Hundred Famous Views of Edo. [AIC 1925.3742](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/26545).
AIC’s description says that the printer applied the gradation of the dark clouds by hand in a scalloped shape rather than the usual straight line. [AIC](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/26545).
observed: A wooden bridge enters at the lower left and leaves the sheet at the right edge. Its piers are cropped by the bottom edge.
Rain falls as hundreds of fine, straight black and gray lines over the whole picture.
The top of the sky is a black cloud that fades in uneven, scalloped edges into gray-blue.
The river is a flat gray-blue. It deepens to Prussian blue along the bottom edge and near the bridge.
The far bank is a band of dark green-gray trees without outlines.
A red vertical cartouche with the series title and a square title panel with colored cloud shapes sit at upper right. A red signature cartouche sits at lower left.
Small figures with straw hats and umbrellas, in yellow, green, and red, lean into the rain on the bridge.
interpretation: The print shows how far the style goes with asymmetry: the subject, the bridge, is pushed to one corner and cut by two edges.
Bokashi carries the weather. It is used at the top and bottom of the sheet, not to model the forms.
borrow: Use a strong diagonal that leaves the frame on two sides, and keep the open area flat.
Put a small saturated red label in a corner of a calm blue-gray field.

images.alt: Color woodblock print. Fine vertical rain lines fall over a gray-blue river and a dark storm cloud. A wooden bridge crosses diagonally from lower left to right, with small travellers under hats and umbrellas. Red title cartouches are at upper right and lower left.
images.caption: Utagawa Hiroshige, Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge and Atake, 1857. [Art Institute of Chicago 1925.3742](https://www.artic.edu/artworks/26545), Clarence Buckingham Collection. CC0.

rights.statement: The Art Institute of Chicago marks the object public domain (`is_public_domain: true`) and releases images of public-domain works under CC0. [AIC open access](https://www.artic.edu/open-access/open-access-images). Hiroshige died in 1858, and the print was published in 1857, so the work is public domain in Japan and the United States.
